what: Human ratings of the Ether grammar V2 closure run (real-closure.json → <id>/base.png, extended.png, unfinished.png, ether-1…5.jpg, noreveal-complete.jpg). Rated by looking. base/extended = the completed figure at the automatic budget, composed with the base vocabulary alone vs with everything the model bound; revealAB = the completed structure with the accepted reveals against without (A transformative · B meaningful · C weak · D unnecessary); judge = the eleven judgements of the brief, each A–D.

vocabulary: Decisions: 6 SUPPORTED, 3 EXTENSION_REQUIRED. Extensions proposed: 3 (2 expressible — both compositions of capabilities the compiler already had by name; 1 refused honestly for three capabilities it lacks). The model bound capabilities directly on 7 of 9 creatures and the extended composition differs from the base one on all 7 — and not one grade moved.
verdict: ONE BLOCKER REMAINS. Open vocabulary does NOT solve the current bottleneck: the model binds the capabilities the compiler offers (outline, curl, lobe, mirror, flare) on nearly every creature, the compositions change, and the grades do not — B/C/D exactly as before. The single structural limitation is the compiler itself: it spends lights on the gesture skeleton (spine ends, transitions, width pairs) and attaches parts as small spikes and quads sized from a length table, so a species — which lives in the silhouette's outline — is never where the lights are. The only figures that read (mermaid, centaur) are the ones whose plan's FLOW already is the silhouette. No creature-specific branch exists anywhere (suite-scanned). Not ready for production; and per the product owner's own next brief the direct image → vision-model extraction is what is tested next, not a further compiler.
loop: every creature completed in the real Ether at eight lights by real taps, came alive and roamed (walks.json: 9/9 alive, 38–65px travelled in the sample) — the loop closes mechanically for every one the accepted reveals draw over the real sky after completion and follow the wanderer while they last, then fade on the reveal's own hold
